name: Progressive
description: Progressive is the second-largest US private-passenger auto insurer (by 2024 premiums written, per the FY2025 10-K, using S&P Global Market Intelligence and A.M. Best data). Customers pay premiums up front for six- or twelve-month policies, Progressive invests the cash until claims are paid, and it profits when premiums exceed claims and expenses (the combined ratio is below 100). It sells both through independent agents and directly online and by phone, and it also insures motorcycles, boats, RVs, homes and renters, and trucks for businesses. It targets a combined ratio of 96 or better and puts profitability ahead of growth. Net premiums written were $83.2B at year-end 2025 and net income was $11.3B.

businessLines.how: Six- and twelve-month policies paid in advance; profit is premiums minus claims and expenses plus investment returns on the float, and pricing is adjusted rate by state to hold the combined ratio near target.
businessLines.description: Personal vehicle (autos, motorcycles, boats, RVs; 96% of the segment) and personal property (homeowners, renters, umbrella, flood).

businessLines.name: Commercial Lines
businessLines.shareBasis: of total net premiums written, 2025 (15% in 2024, 16% in 2023)
businessLines.how: Annual policies for businesses' trucks and vans priced on risk; same premium-minus-claims economics as personal auto.
businessLines.description: Commercial auto for small businesses, mostly for-hire transportation, contractors, tow and business auto; also business-related general liability and property.
